theme: The High Priestly Prayer, “that they may be one”
readingInstruction: Read John 17:1-26. This is the longest prayer of Jesus in the Bible, often called the High Priestly Prayer. He prays for himself, for his disciples, and for all who will believe through their word. You are overhearing the Son pray for you. Read it slowly.
settingTheScene: Jesus has finished teaching in the upper room. Before crossing the Kidron valley to the garden, he lifts his eyes to heaven and prays aloud, so that his disciples can hear. The prayer has three parts: for his own glorification (vv. 1 to 5), for the eleven disciples (vv. 6 to 19), and for all future believers (vv. 20 to 26). It is a rare glimpse into the intimate relationship between the Son and the Father, and into what Jesus wants for his people.
observation: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son that the Son may glorify you” (17:1).
“And this is eternal life, that they know you the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent” (17:3).
“I glorified you on earth, having accomplished the work that you gave me to do” (17:4).
“I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil one” (17:15).
“Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth” (17:17).
“That they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in us” (17:21).
“Father, I desire that they also, whom you have given me, may be with me where I am, to see my glory” (17:24).
“That the love with which you have loved me may be in them, and I in them” (17:26).
interpretation:
Jesus begins by praying for himself, but his request is that the Son may glorify the Father. He has authority over all flesh so that he may give eternal life to all whom the Father has given him. Then he defines eternal life: “that they know you the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” Eternal life is not just endless time. It is a relationship, knowing God through Christ. He says he has finished the work he was given, and asks to be restored to the glory he had with the Father before the world existed. The Son who is about to die speaks as if it is finished, because it is certain.

Then he prays for the eleven. They are the Father’s gift to him, and he has given them the Father’s word. He prays, “I am not praying for the world but for those whom you have given me.” He asks that the Father keep them in his name, that they may be one. He does not ask that they be taken out of the world, but kept from the evil one. They are in the world but not of the world. And he asks, “Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.” To be sanctified is to be set apart and made holy, and it happens through the Word. Then, “As you sent me into the world, so I have sent them into the world.” The disciples are sent as he was sent.

The third part is for you, if you believe. “I do not ask for these only, but also for those who will believe in me through their word.” Jesus prayed for every future believer. He asks that they all may be one, “just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you.” The unity of believers reflects the unity of the Father and Son, and its purpose is mission: “so that the world may believe that you have sent me.” A divided church makes the gospel harder to believe. A united church is a witness.

He ends with the destination: “Father, I desire that they also, whom you have given me, may be with me where I am, to see my glory.” The goal of salvation is to be with Christ and to see him. And he says that the love of the Father for the Son will be in them. We are loved with the same love.

Notice how the prayer shows the security of the believer. The Son is praying for us, and the Father always hears him. As Romans 8:34 says, he is at the right hand of God, interceding for us.
connection: Exodus 28 and Leviticus 16 describe the high priest’s work. Hebrews 4:14-16 and 7:23-25 say Jesus is our great high priest who always lives to make intercession. Romans 8:34 says Christ intercedes for us. Isaiah 53:12 says he makes intercession for the transgressors. Ephesians 4:1-6 calls for the unity of the Spirit. Luke 22:32 records his prayer for Peter. 1 John 5:20 says to know the true God is eternal life. Revelation 21:3 promises that God will dwell with his people.
application:
Remember that Jesus has prayed for you by name. Write one sentence about what that means.

Pray this prayer back: for your own sanctification by the word, for your church’s unity, and for the world to believe.

Reach out to a Christian from another tradition or community this week, as a sign of unity.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for praying for you before you were born.
Thank God that eternal life is knowing him.
Ask him to make you one with his people.
